ehit.l: How far the thrombus extends. A bare "I" is not accepted - choose Ia or Ib, where Ib is the original 2006 class I [Ia = Thrombus without propagation into the deep vein, peripheral to the superficial epigastric vein. Ib = Thrombus without propagation into the deep vein, central to the superficial epigastric vein, up to and including the deep vein junction. II = Propagation into the adjacent deep vein, occupying less than 50 percent of the deep vein lumen. III = Propagation into the adjacent deep vein, occupying more than 50 percent of the lumen, but not occlusive. IV = Occlusive deep vein thrombus contiguous with the treated superficial vein.]

ehra-af.l: Whether atrial fibrillation causes any symptoms. NO gives class 1 outright.

Effect on normal daily activity. The discriminator everywhere except the 2a/2b boundary [not-affected = Normal daily activity NOT affected; affected = Normal daily activity affected; discontinued = Normal daily activity discontinued]
Whether the patient is TROUBLED by the symptoms. Read ONLY when daily activity is not affected: it is the entire 2a versus 2b split, and the one place this scale turns on a subjective judgment.
